  "text": "At the alterations shop, Helen laid a wool coat across the counter.

“The lining,” she said.

The woman turned back a sleeve. Two fingers came through the split.

“Both sides?”

“I think so.”

The woman checked the other sleeve, then smoothed the coat flat.

“I can patch it. New lining would cost more.”

“A patch is fine.”

“What colour?”

“Whatever you've got.”

The woman looked up.

“Brown, then.”

Helen nodded. Behind the counter, a radio was giving the traffic report. There was a delay on the road to the hospital, though the announcer didn't say which direction.

“Name?”

Helen gave it.

“And a number.”

She started with the old house number, stopped, and gave her mobile instead.

“Friday,” the woman said.

“There's no hurry.”

“Friday is when I do linings.”

Outside, Helen put her hands in her cardigan pockets. She had forgotten to empty the coat. In the left pocket there would be a tissue and perhaps a receipt. In the right, the small flat stone her grandson had given her at the beach.

She went back inside.

“Something in the pocket,” she said.

The woman lifted the coat from a chair.

Helen found the stone. It was grey now, without the stripes it had shown when wet.

“Got it?”

“Yes. Thank you.”

At the bus stop, she rubbed it with her thumb. When the bus arrived, she needed that hand for her pass. She put the stone in her cardigan pocket and held the pocket closed until she was seated."
